clue.text: Person making dough around clubs as supporter

indicators.note: the baker's letters are placed around the card suit, enclosing it

parts.note: a baker makes bread dough
C is the abbreviation for the card suit

explanation.surface: A baker who takes up golf, or joins clubs, turns out to be someone's financial backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough hints at money, which fits the supporter sense, but here it is literal bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer is someone who gives support, especially financial, to a venture or person.

clue.text: Reserve currency no longer used — reminder placed in work

parts.note: to book is to reserve
the Deutschmark was replaced by the euro

explanation.surface: Setting aside an old currency, with a note slipped into a project.
explanation.walkthrough: Work here is a literary work, a book, where the reminder marks your page.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmark is a strip placed in a book to mark the reader's place for later.

clue.text: Arrest for threatening announcement by player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to halt or stop progress
second meaning: what a chess player calls when attacking the king

explanation.walkthrough: Arrest suggests police, and player an actor or sportsman; the second sense is chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to stop or restrain, and in chess it announces a direct attack on the opposing king.

clue.text: Repeating speech so boring, left 50 per cent out throughout

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its first half, leaving only its second half

parts.note: the word speech keeps its back three letters
the word so keeps its last letter
the word boring keeps its back three letters

explanation.surface: A speech so dull the listener tuned out half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word keeps only its back half: speech, so and boring each drop their opening half.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoing means reproducing a sound or words again, which is repeating them.

clue.text: After church, primate left for another place of worship

indicators.note: the primate and left come after church, so those letters follow it in the answer

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An ape leaves one church and heads off to worship somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, distinct from the main church.

clue.text: Regular visitor somewhat put in shade

indicators.note: the phrase for somewhat is placed inside the word for shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a bit means somewhat, as in a bit tired

explanation.surface: A frequent guest who is rather overshadowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Put in shade suggests being overshadowed; it is really a container instruction with a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is someone who frequents a particular place, a regular customer.

clue.text: Showing a bit of light in entrance

indicators.note: the beam sits within the word for entrance

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway
a ray is a thin beam of light

explanation.surface: A little light shining in through a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or representation, a showing of someone or something.

clue.text: Shed adjoining building slowly covering area

indicators.note: the musical word wraps round the area

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: A shed slowly being built over a patch of ground next to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shelter with a sloping roof propped against an existing wall.

clue.text: United's defensive blunder in tie

indicators.note: the blunder sits inside the word for tie

parts.note: to tether is to tie up an animal
OG is short for own goal, a defender's error in football

explanation.surface: A football report: Manchester United concede an own goal in a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like the football club and tie like a drawn game; tie is a tether, and OG is the football abbreviation for an own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are joined or acting as one are united, which is the same as being together.

clue.text: Part of Bible filling clergymen briefly with joy

indicators.note: the joy fills the shortened clergymen, sitting inside them

parts.note: Rev is the short title for a reverend
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A Bible passage that delights the vicars.
explanation.walkthrough: Revelation is often referred to in the plural as Revelations, the final book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelations is the familiar name for the Book of Revelation, the last book of the Bible.

clue.text: Chap who delivers orders from outlaw holding weapon

indicators.note: the word for outlaw holds the weapon inside it

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gang leader with a gun barks orders at his men.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivers orders sounds like commanding, but a barman delivers drinks that customers have ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves the drinks customers ask for, so he literally brings their orders.

clue.text: In a frenzy, brief reassurance about my condition

parts.note: what you say about your own state, as in '(I) am well'
OK is a short word of reassurance

explanation.surface: Someone frantically insisting they're fine when they plainly aren't.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'I am OK' with the I left off: AM then OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave wildly and out of control, as in a frenzy.

clue.text: Variety of native tree that's deep-rooted

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of these two words take another arrangement

parts.note: these two words supply the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of native tree whose roots go deep into the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Deep-rooted reads as describing the tree, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inveterate habit is long-established and firmly ingrained, as if deep-rooted.

clue.text: Where journalists may be found after crowd largely dispersed

parts.note: to press is to crowd, and a press is a throng

indicators.note: the letters of largely are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the seven letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reporters gather once the crowd has mostly gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: Largely looks like a quantity word modifying dispersed, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The press gallery is the seating area in a parliament reserved for reporters.

clue.text: Turner including a ketch's bow sail

indicators.note: the word for turner takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a spinner is something that turns
taken as written

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of the ketch's name

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat; its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A painter like Turner depicting a sail at the bow of a ketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J.M.W. Turner, but here it is anything that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is a large balloon-shaped sail set at the front of a yacht running before the wind.

clue.text: Listed some comrades I met initially going the wrong way

indicators.note: the run of letters is read in reverse order
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run within it

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of comrades, I, met and the start of initially

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a few comrades they met who went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Initially looks like a first-letters signal but supplies just its own opening letter to the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Itemised means set out item by item, as in a detailed list.

clue.text: Trait in a clue that's awful, not using words clearly

indicators.note: an awful version of the phrase is a mess, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: these four words supply the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter's critic complains about a badly worded clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inarticulate cannot express themselves fluently or coherently in speech.

clue.text: Workers rising within a unit in plant

indicators.note: the reversed workers sit inside the article plus unit

parts.note: taken as written
one is a single unit

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Workers rising up as a single group inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a factory where workers might rise up, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family, also called windflower.

clue.text: Where Englishman's at home, it's said, including one part of Spain

indicators.note: the place takes the numeral inside it

parts.words: Where Englishman's at home, it's said
parts.note: the proverb says an Englishman's home is his castle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A proverb about English homes, with one area of Spain thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: It's said points to the proverb, not to a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile is a historic region and former kingdom of central Spain.

clue.text: Shed in swampy area

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cast off, as a snake its skin
second meaning: a bog or quagmire

explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like a garden building in a marsh; it is the verb, pronounced to rhyme with stuff, while the swamp rhymes with plough.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake sloughs off its skin, and a slough is also a muddy, boggy patch of ground.

clue.text: Soil inside grave I removed? That's defamatory

indicators.note: the soil goes inside what remains of grave
the letter I is taken away from the word for grave

parts.note: grave means serious
the letter I itself, taken as written
land is soil, as in working the land

explanation.surface: A gravedigger's question about soil, followed by an accusation of libel.
explanation.walkthrough: Grave suggests a burial plot with soil in it, but it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanderous remarks are spoken falsehoods that damage someone's good name, which is defamation.

clue.text: After cold, ring doctor to sort out shock, in a way

definitions.text: sort out shock, in a way

indicators.note: ring and doctor come after cold, so their letters follow it

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: After catching a cold, you call the doctor to deal with the shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock seems medical, but here it is a shock of hair, untangled with a comb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick mass of hair, and combing it tidies and untangles it.

clue.text: Hiding-place pronounced ready

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for ready money matches the hiding-place

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A hideout declared prepared for use.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: British slang for available money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or valuables, and so a hiding-place.

clue.text: Silly person that entrusts nest egg to others

definitions.text: that entrusts nest egg to others
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the bird that lays its eggs in other birds' nests

explanation.walkthrough: Nest egg suggests savings handed to a fund manager; the cuckoo literally leaves its egg for other birds to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuckoo is a brood parasite, and the word is also informal for a crazy or foolish person.

clue.text: Legal actions that may be carried on by boarder

definitions.text: that may be carried on by boarder

parts.note: a suit is a legal action, the first of two
a case is another legal action, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A list of lawsuits that might be pursued by a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: Carried on suggests continuing a lawsuit, and boarder a lodger; really it is luggage carried onto a plane by someone boarding.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is luggage a passenger may take with them as cabin baggage when boarding.

clue.text: Line dividing women's quarters in New York district

indicators.note: the line splits the quarters by sitting inside the word

parts.note: a harem is the women's section of a Muslim household

explanation.surface: A partition separating the women's area within a building in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a neighbourhood in northern Manhattan, famous for its African-American culture.

clue.text: Experience confinement, kept under observation

definitions.meaning: first meaning, as two words: to undergo being detained
second meaning: watched, the past of the verb meaning to look at

explanation.surface: A detainee is locked up and watched by guards.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer means being detained; as one it is the past of behold.
explanation.definitionFit: To behold is to look at or watch, so something beheld has been seen and observed.
